$comment: The request bodies the API sends to the inference service, and the response shapes it expects back. Read from BOTH sides: the API's test asserts its client produces exactly these, and the inference service's test asserts its routes accept them. A cross-language contract cannot be held by a shared type, so it is held by a shared example.

requests.name: embed with display adjustments
requests.note: RULE-089. The browser sends this body; the API renders the adjusted image and adds `pixels`, a base64 PNG, before forwarding. It is listed rather than written out because its value comes from the image on disk -- the TypeScript suite checks it is present and non-empty, and the Python suite posts this body without it, which is the path where the service reads the file itself.

requests.name: embed the processed view
requests.note: RULE-089 with the processing chain. Legacy's rescale, thresholds and FFT replace the image its adjustments apply to, so Operate On View segments the PROCESSED view. `processing` is the pixels route's own query string: the API renders through it and forwards it, because the service keys its encodings on the whole view. Opaque to the service.

requests.name: start a propagation
requests.$comment: 202, not 200: the service accepted a job that runs for minutes. Both sides keep it -- an API that answered 200 would tell the browser the work was done. Frame numbers are POSITIONS in `sequence` and never file names, which is RULE-017: legacy names each staged frame after its position in its own list and skips one it cannot read without renumbering, so every frame after a gap comes back attributed to the image before it. The reference MASKS travel in `objects`, separately from `references`, because one frame can carry several objects and the service needs both answers. They are the user's own annotations: legacy seeds with `add_new_mask`, and re-deriving a prompt from someone's polygon gives a mask close to theirs and not theirs.

requests.name: find archetypes in a sequence
requests.$comment: One request and one answer rather than a job, unlike propagation: a single pass that embeds every frame once. There is no per-frame result to stream, and a partial answer would not help if there were -- half the clusters is not half the suggestions, it is a different set.

requests.name: load a model now
requests.$comment: Legacy's Load (CP-49): the model in memory now rather than on first use, freeing any other. The same manifest and SHA-256 check as first use; nothing is fetched.

requests.name: unload a model
requests.$comment: Legacy's Unload (CP-49): the model out of memory and the CUDA cache emptied. With no body, whatever is loaded.
